native_mechanisms: Per-road runner relaxation: lay a stick on the far heap equal to the home heap's current ember plus that road's notched length (edge relaxation dist[u]+w).
One land-wide synchronous 'throw': all heaps resolve their pending sticks in a single global round, each heap keeping its shortest sliver as its new ember and discarding (burning) the rest.
Garrison sealing: once a heap's ember is unchanged between consecutive throws, fix its distance permanently and stop its outgoing runners (plus marking never-lit heaps as unreachable).
core_technique: Round-synchronous pull-based Bellman-Ford over a reverse-CSR graph with double-buffered dist arrays, per-node min-reduction each round, an active/changed frontier flag to skip unchanged sources, and OpenMP parallelism — with a guarded escape to binary-heap Dijkstra only for sparse/large (n>4000 and avg degree<8) inputs.
